evidence_tiers.T1: Licensed medicine. Published label dosing and regulatory safety data.
evidence_tiers.T2: Human RCT data exists but not licensed for this use, or licensed only recently/regionally.
evidence_tiers.T3: Limited human data - small studies, single research group, or licensed only in some jurisdictions.
evidence_tiers.T4: Animal data only. Human dosing figures are community extrapolation with no trial basis.
evidence_tiers.T5: Essentially no data. Circulating dose figures are forum folklore with no traceable source.
evidence_tiers.TX: Excluded. Dosing deliberately not provided - see the safety field for the specific reason.

field_notes.established: What controlled evidence actually supports. Deliberately kept separate from reported effects.
field_notes.reported: Community-reported effects. These are not evidence. Placebo, concurrent training and diet changes, and vendor-driven expectation all contaminate this field heavily.
field_notes.confidence: How much weight the dose figure itself deserves - not how well the compound works.

compounds.name: Semaglutide
compounds.human_data: Extensive. STEP (obesity), SUSTAIN (T2D), SELECT (cardiovascular outcomes). Licensed globally.
compounds.dose: Label titration: 0.25 mg weekly x4wk, 0.5 x4wk, 1.0 x4wk, 1.7 x4wk, 2.4 mg maintenance (Wegovy). Ozempic caps at 2.0 mg.
compounds.frequency: Once weekly, subcutaneous, same day each week.
compounds.cycle: Not cycled. Continuous therapy. Weight regain after cessation is well documented (~two-thirds regained within a year in STEP-1 extension).
established: ~15% mean body weight reduction at 68wk (STEP-1)
HbA1c reduction
20% MACE reduction in established CVD (SELECT)
reported: Appetite suppression, 'food noise' reduction
Reduced alcohol intake
Improved inflammatory markers
compounds.mechanism: GLP-1 receptor agonist. Delays gastric emptying, central satiety signalling, glucose-dependent insulinotropic effect.
safety: GI: nausea, vomiting, constipation - dose-limiting
Gallbladder disease, pancreatitis
Rodent thyroid C-cell tumours; contraindicated in MEN2/MTC history
Significant lean mass loss without resistance training and adequate protein
Gastroparesis; anaesthesia aspiration risk - disclose before surgery
monitor: Body composition, not just scale weight

compounds.name: Tirzepatide
compounds.human_data: Extensive. SURMOUNT (obesity), SURPASS (T2D). Licensed.
compounds.dose: Label titration: 2.5 mg weekly x4wk, then 5, 7.5, 10, 12.5, 15 mg, each step held 4wk. Maintenance commonly 10-15 mg.
established: ~22.5% mean weight reduction at 72wk, 15 mg arm (SURMOUNT-1)
Superior HbA1c reduction vs semaglutide (SURPASS-2)
reported: Stronger appetite effect than semaglutide at equivalent titration stage
Better GI tolerability per-unit-efficacy, reported inconsistently
compounds.mechanism: Dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonist.
safety: Same GI, gallbladder, pancreatitis and C-cell profile as semaglutide
Lean mass loss
Gastroparesis / anaesthesia risk

compounds.name: Retatrutide
compounds.human_data: Phase 2 published (NEJM, n=338). Phase 3 TRIUMPH programme ongoing/reporting. Not licensed anywhere.
compounds.dose: DISPUTED. Trial arms ran 1-12 mg weekly. Commonly cited schedules conflict: 2>4>8>12, 1>2>4>6>9>12, and 2>4>6>9>12 all appear in secondary sources. Each step held ~4wk. No consensus schedule exists outside the trial protocols.
established: ~24.2% weight reduction at 48wk (Phase 2, 12 mg)
~28.7% reported at 68wk in Phase 3
reported: Strongest appetite effect of the incretin class
Noticeable thermogenic/warmth effect attributed to glucagon agonism
compounds.mechanism: Triple GLP-1 / GIP / glucagon receptor agonist. Glucagon arm adds energy expenditure.
safety: Dysesthesia (skin tingling/burning) ~21% in Phase 3 - class-distinctive
Resting HR increase ~5-10 bpm
Glucagon agonism can raise hepatic glucose output; glycaemic effects less predictable
All GLP-1 class risks apply
Investigational - no post-marketing safety surveillance exists
compounds.confidence: medium - dose steps genuinely unsettled in public sources

compounds.name: Survodutide
compounds.human_data: Phase 2 published (Boehringer/Zealand). Phase 3 ongoing. Not licensed.
compounds.dose: Trials used up to 6.0 mg weekly with slow escalation over ~20wk.
established: ~14.9% weight reduction at 46wk, 4.8 mg arm (Phase 2)
Phase 2 signal in MASH resolution
reported: Thermogenic effect similar in character to retatrutide
compounds.mechanism: Dual GLP-1 / glucagon receptor agonist.
safety: High GI adverse event rate in Phase 2, notably at faster escalation
HR increase
Hepatic glucose output effects

compounds.name: Mazdutide
compounds.human_data: Phase 2/3 primarily in China (Innovent, licensed from Lilly as IBI362). Regulatory status is China-first.
compounds.dose: Trials used 3.0, 4.5, 6.0 and 9.0 mg weekly with escalation.
established: ~14-15% weight reduction at higher doses in Chinese Phase 2/3 cohorts
reported: Appetite suppression comparable to semaglutide at matched stage
compounds.mechanism: Dual GLP-1 / glucagon (oxyntomodulin analogue).
safety: Standard incretin GI profile
Trial populations largely Chinese - generalisability to other populations not established

compounds.name: Cagrilintide
compounds.human_data: Phase 2 monotherapy and Phase 3 as part of CagriSema. Not licensed as monotherapy.
compounds.dose: Trials used 0.3-4.5 mg weekly, most commonly titrated to 2.4 mg.
established: ~10-11% weight reduction as monotherapy at 26wk
Additive to semaglutide in CagriSema
reported: Satiety quality described as different from GLP-1 - fullness rather than appetite absence
compounds.mechanism: Long-acting amylin analogue. Amylin signals meal termination and slows gastric emptying via a separate pathway to GLP-1.
safety: Nausea, particularly during escalation
Injection site reactions more common than GLP-1 class

compounds.name: CJC-1295 with DAC
compounds.human_data: Small Phase 1 PK/PD studies (n<100) published ~2006. Development discontinued. Never licensed.
compounds.dose: Community range 1-2 mg per week, given as a single dose or split into two.
compounds.frequency: Once or twice weekly. The DAC (drug affinity complex) binds albumin, giving a half-life of roughly 6-8 days.
compounds.cycle: Community practice runs 8-12wk on, 4wk off, largely by analogy to other GH-axis compounds rather than from data.
established: Dose-dependent increase in GH and IGF-1 lasting 6+ days in Phase 1
reported: Improved sleep depth
Skin and connective tissue changes
Slow recomposition over months
compounds.mechanism: Long-acting GHRH analogue. Raises the GH baseline continuously.
safety: Continuous elevation abolishes normal pulsatile GH secretion - long-term consequence unstudied
Water retention, carpal tunnel symptoms, joint ache
Insulin resistance at sustained high IGF-1
IGF-1 elevation and cancer risk is a genuine open question, not a settled one

compounds.name: CJC-1295 without DAC (Mod GRF 1-29)
compounds.human_data: None specific to this analogue. Inferred from sermorelin/GHRH literature.
compounds.dose: Community range 100 mcg per administration.
compounds.frequency: One to three times daily. Half-life ~30 min, so it produces a pulse rather than a plateau.
established: Nothing specific to this molecule in humans
reported: Sleep quality when dosed pre-bed
Preferred over DAC version specifically because it preserves pulsatility
compounds.mechanism: GHRH(1-29) with four substitutions for protease resistance, including Leu27 replacing the oxidation-prone methionine.
safety: Injection site flushing
Milder water retention than DAC version
Same IGF-1 uncertainty

compounds.name: Sermorelin
compounds.human_data: Was licensed (Geref) for paediatric GH deficiency and as a diagnostic. Commercially withdrawn, not for safety.
compounds.dose: Historical label: 0.2-0.3 mg. Community adult use sits in the same range.
compounds.frequency: Once daily, typically at night to align with natural GH pulse.
compounds.cycle: Continuous in licensed use. Community practice cycles 3-6 months.
established: Stimulates endogenous GH release
Diagnostic utility in GH deficiency
reported: Sleep quality
Gentler subjective profile than GHRPs
compounds.mechanism: GHRH(1-29), the natural fragment. Retains Met27 and so is oxidation-sensitive.
safety: Injection site reaction most common
Requires intact pituitary
Headache, flushing

compounds.name: Tesamorelin
compounds.human_data: Licensed (Egrifta) for HIV-associated lipodystrophy. Phase 3 data published.
compounds.dose: Label: 2 mg daily subcutaneous. (A 1.4 mg F8 formulation also exists.)
compounds.cycle: Continuous in licensed use; benefit reverses on cessation.
established: ~15-18% visceral adipose tissue reduction over 26wk
Effect is VAT-selective; does not reduce subcutaneous fat comparably
Reduces liver fat in some cohorts
reported: Cognitive effects at the margins - weak signal
Used off-label for VAT in non-HIV populations without supporting trial data
compounds.mechanism: Stabilised GHRH analogue.
safety: Glucose intolerance - clinically significant, appears in label
Arthralgia, peripheral oedema
Injection site reactions common
Aggregates readily in solution - inspect before every draw
monitor: Fasting glucose / HbA1c - this one genuinely matters

compounds.name: Ipamorelin
compounds.human_data: Small early-phase work on postoperative ileus, abandoned. No efficacy or safety data at community doses.
compounds.dose: Community range 100-300 mcg per administration.
compounds.frequency: One to three times daily; commonly pre-bed and post-training.
established: GH release in animal models with minimal cortisol/prolactin effect
reported: Sleep depth
Mild recovery improvement
Preferred for being the 'clean' GHRP - no hunger, no prolactin
compounds.mechanism: Selective ghrelin receptor (GHS-R1a) agonist.
safety: Head rush / flushing shortly after injection
Receptor desensitisation with continuous use is the rationale for cycling
IGF-1 elevation uncertainty

compounds.name: GHRP-2
compounds.human_data: Some human PK work; used diagnostically in Japan. No long-term data.
compounds.dose: Community range 100-300 mcg.
established: Potent GH release in acute human studies
reported: Mild appetite increase
Stronger GH pulse than ipamorelin
compounds.mechanism: Ghrelin receptor agonist, less selective than ipamorelin.
safety: Cortisol and prolactin elevation at higher doses
Desensitisation
Appetite stimulation may be unwanted alongside incretins
monitor: Prolactin if run long or high

compounds.name: GHRP-6
compounds.human_data: Limited acute human PK. No long-term data.
compounds.dose: Community range 100-300 mcg.
established: GH release; pronounced appetite stimulation
reported: Strong hunger within ~20 min - used deliberately during bulking phases
compounds.mechanism: Ghrelin receptor agonist. Most ghrelin-like of the GHRPs in appetite effect.
safety: Marked appetite stimulation
Cortisol and prolactin elevation
Desensitisation

compounds.name: Hexarelin
compounds.human_data: Some cardiac-focused human work in the 1990s. Abandoned.
compounds.dose: Community range 100 mcg.
compounds.cycle: Short. 2-3wk on is the common recommendation because desensitisation is faster than the other GHRPs.
established: Potent acute GH release
Direct cardiac effects independent of GH in animal models
reported: Strongest GH pulse of the GHRP group, and the fastest to stop working
compounds.mechanism: Ghrelin receptor agonist, highest potency of the group.
safety: Rapid, pronounced receptor desensitisation
Cortisol and prolactin elevation more marked than GHRP-2

compounds.name: BPC-157
compounds.human_data: None published. Every efficacy claim traces to rodent work from a small number of research groups, largely one Croatian lab.
compounds.dose: Community range 200-500 mcg per day. Systemic vs local injection is debated with no data either way.
compounds.cycle: 4-8wk, tied to the injury being addressed rather than a fixed schedule.
established: Tendon, ligament, muscle and gut healing acceleration in rodents
Nothing in humans
reported: Tendinopathy and soft tissue recovery - the dominant claim
Gut symptom relief, including in IBD and NSAID-related irritation
Reduced joint pain
compounds.mechanism: Proposed: VEGFR2 signalling, angiogenesis, nitric oxide pathway modulation, growth factor upregulation. Mechanism is not settled.
safety: No human safety data at all - this is the honest position
Angiogenic activity is theoretically undesirable in the presence of an undiagnosed malignancy
Banned by WADA
monitor: Subjective function; there is no biomarker to follow
compounds.confidence: low - very high community confidence, very low evidence base. The gap between those two is the largest on this list.

compounds.name: TB-500 (Thymosin Beta-4)
compounds.human_data: Thymosin beta-4 itself reached Phase 2 for dry eye and dermal wounds. TB-500 as sold is a fragment, not the full protein, and has no human data.
compounds.dose: Community loading 2-2.5 mg twice weekly for 4-6wk, then 2-2.5 mg every 1-2wk maintenance.
established: Actin sequestration, cell migration and angiogenesis in preclinical models
Full-length Tβ4 showed some corneal wound healing signal in trials
reported: Systemic flexibility and 'looseness'
Muscle and tendon recovery
Frequently stacked with BPC-157
compounds.mechanism: Actin-binding peptide fragment; promotes cell migration and angiogenesis.
safety: No human safety data
Angiogenic - same theoretical malignancy concern
Banned by WADA

compounds.name: KPV
compounds.human_data: None. Rodent colitis models only.
compounds.dose: Community range 200-500 mcg per day.
compounds.frequency: Once daily. Oral/enteric routes are also used for gut-specific intent.
established: Anti-inflammatory effect in rodent colitis
reported: Gut inflammation
Skin inflammation
compounds.mechanism: C-terminal tripeptide of alpha-MSH. Retains anti-inflammatory activity without melanocortin receptor pigmentation effects.
safety: No human data
Generally reported as well tolerated, which is not the same as being safe

compounds.name: GHK-Cu
compounds.human_data: Substantial for topical/cosmetic use. Essentially none for injection.
compounds.dose: Community injectable 1-2 mg per day. Topical is the far better-evidenced route.
compounds.cycle: Short courses, 2-4wk, because of copper accumulation concern.
established: Topical: collagen synthesis, skin appearance, wound healing
Injectable: no controlled human data
reported: Skin quality, hair
Connective tissue
compounds.mechanism: Copper-binding tripeptide. Modulates collagen and metalloproteinase expression.
safety: Subcutaneous injection is notably painful and can leave staining
Systemic copper load - repeated high dosing risks copper accumulation; copper toxicity is real and affects liver and neurological function
Topical route avoids this entirely and has better evidence
monitor: Serum copper and ceruloplasmin if injecting at dose or repeatedly

compounds.name: AHK-Cu
compounds.human_data: None beyond cosmetic formulation work.
compounds.dose: No established figure. Community use mirrors GHK-Cu.
established: Nothing in humans
reported: Hair growth, mostly from topical cosmetic context
compounds.mechanism: Copper-binding tripeptide, proposed follicular effects.
safety: Same copper accumulation concern as GHK-Cu
No injectable data whatsoever

compounds.name: GLOW (GHK-Cu + TB-500 + BPC-157)
compounds.human_data: None. A vendor-created blend, not a studied product.
compounds.dose: Blend is dosed as a unit; component doses are fixed by the vendor's ratio and may not match what you would choose individually.
established: Nothing - no blend has been studied
reported: Skin, hair and recovery effects attributed to the combination
compounds.mechanism: See individual components.
safety: Fixed ratio removes your ability to titrate any single component
Copper accumulation from the GHK-Cu fraction
Compounding of three separate no-human-data compounds

compounds.name: KLOW (BPC-157 + GHK-Cu + TB-500 + KPV)
compounds.human_data: None. Vendor blend.
compounds.dose: Dosed as a unit at the vendor's fixed ratio.
established: Nothing
reported: Same claims as GLOW plus gut/anti-inflammatory from the KPV fraction
compounds.mechanism: See individual components.
safety: Four compounds, fixed ratio, no titration control
Copper accumulation

compounds.name: BPC-157 + TB-500 blend
compounds.human_data: None.
compounds.dose: Vendor blend at 1:1. Community dosing follows the individual compound ranges.
compounds.frequency: Once daily to twice weekly depending on the ratio drawn.
established: Nothing
reported: The most common repair stack; claimed synergy is assertion, not finding
compounds.mechanism: See individual components.
safety: Combined no-data profile of both

compounds.name: Melanotan 1 (Afamelanotide)
compounds.human_data: Licensed as Scenesse, a subcutaneous implant, for erythropoietic protoporphyria. Injectable community use is a different route and product.
compounds.dose: Community loading around 0.5-1 mg per day until desired pigmentation, then maintenance 1-2x weekly.
compounds.cycle: Load then maintain; pigmentation fades over weeks after stopping.
established: Photoprotection in EPP (licensed indication)
Reliable melanogenesis
reported: Tanning with reduced UV exposure
Fewer side effects than Melanotan 2 - notably no significant erectile or nausea effect
compounds.mechanism: Alpha-MSH analogue, melanocortin receptor agonist, principally MC1R.
safety: Existing naevi darken and may change appearance, which can mask or mimic melanoma
Requires baseline and ongoing skin surveillance
Nausea, flushing during loading
monitor: Dermatological skin check before starting and periodically - this is not optional advice

compounds.name: Melanotan 2
compounds.human_data: Early trials abandoned. No licensed product. Case reports dominate the literature.
compounds.dose: Community loading 250-500 mcg per day, then maintenance 1-2x weekly.
established: Melanogenesis
Erectile effect - the PT-141 spinoff came from this observation
reported: Tanning, appetite suppression, spontaneous erections, libido increase
compounds.mechanism: Non-selective melanocortin agonist (MC1R, MC3R, MC4R).
safety: Case reports of melanoma and rapidly changing naevi in users - the strongest safety signal of any compound on this list outside the excluded ones
Priapism
Nausea, flushing, and marked blood pressure changes during loading
Non-selective receptor action is why the side effect profile is broad
monitor: Dermatological review before and during use
Any changing mole warrants immediate assessment
compounds.confidence: low - and the safety concerns here are better evidenced than the benefits

compounds.name: PT-141 (Bremelanotide)
compounds.human_data: Licensed as Vyleesi for hypoactive sexual desire disorder in premenopausal women. Phase 3 data published.
compounds.dose: Label: 1.75 mg subcutaneous as needed, at least 45 min before anticipated activity. Community male use often 0.5-2 mg.
compounds.frequency: As needed. Label limits to one dose per 24h and no more than 8 per month.
established: Improved sexual desire scores in licensed indication
reported: Libido effect distinct from PDE5 inhibitors - central rather than vascular
Effect onset 1-3h, duration variable
compounds.mechanism: Melanocortin receptor agonist acting centrally on MC4R.
safety: Nausea is the dominant adverse effect - occurred in roughly 40% in trials
Transient blood pressure increase and HR decrease; label cautions in uncontrolled hypertension or CVD
Flushing, headache
Focal hyperpigmentation with frequent use - the reason for the monthly cap

compounds.name: Epithalon (AEDG)
compounds.human_data: Russian clinical work from Khavinson's group over decades. Not independently replicated outside Russia; methodology and reporting standards differ from Western trial norms.
compounds.dose: Community protocol 5-10 mg per day.
compounds.cycle: 10-20 consecutive days, repeated once or twice per year. This short-course-annual pattern is the defining feature.
established: Telomerase activation in cell culture
Russian cohort claims of mortality and functional benefit that have not been independently reproduced
reported: Sleep quality
Subjective wellbeing
Longevity intent - unfalsifiable at individual level
compounds.mechanism: Tetrapeptide, proposed pineal regulation and telomerase induction.
safety: Telomerase activation cuts both ways - it is also a mechanism of cellular immortalisation. This is a genuine theoretical concern that the longevity framing tends to omit
Little safety data outside the originating group

compounds.mechanism: Thymus peptide complex. Russian clinical use in immune support. Proposed mechanism is peptide-DNA interaction regulating tissue-specific gene expression; this model is not accepted outside the originating group.
safety: Minimal reported toxicity, but also minimal scrutiny

compounds.name: Semax

compounds.name: 5-Amino-1MQ
